title: Therapeutic massage
what: A massage therapist works your muscles with their hands. It eases tension, improves blood flow, and helps you recover.
why: For back and neck pain, after injuries and surgery, for tight muscles, and during recovery from illness.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes per session, and a course is usually about 10 sessions
tell_doctor: If you have a fever or a cold
Blood clots in your veins or varicose veins
Heart problems or blood pressure problems
If you have or have had a tumor

prepare.title: Referral
prepare.text: Massage is usually prescribed by a doctor, who says which area to work on.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not eat a heavy meal for an hour before and right after the session.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Take a shower. Do not put on cream before the session, unless the therapist asks you to.

bring: A towel or sheet, if asked
steps: The therapist asks how you feel and where it hurts
You undress to uncover the area and lie on the table
The therapist puts on oil or cream
First gentle stroking, then kneading of the muscles
At the end, gentle movements again, and you rest a little
feel: Tight spots can feel unpleasant. This is normal
If it really hurts, tell the therapist right away
After the first sessions, your muscles may ache for 1 to 2 days
after: Do not get up quickly. Lie still for a couple of minutes
Drink water if you want to
Do not go straight out into the cold
If you feel worse after a session, tell your doctor

faq.a: No. It can feel unpleasant, but strong pain is a sign to stop. Tell the therapist.

faq.q: How many sessions do I need?
faq.a: Usually a course of about 10 sessions. The doctor decides the exact number.
